questions.question_text: A woman develops an obstetric fistula following prolonged obstructed labour and experiences continuous leakage of urine. Which rehabilitation intervention should form part of her long-term care after appropriate surgical assessment?

choices.text: Restricting her contact with family members until the leakage stops
Providing psychosocial support, continence care, and assistance with community reintegration
Advising her to discontinue all physical activities permanently
Managing the condition exclusively with traditional herbal preparations

questions.rationale: Rehabilitation after obstetric fistula should address physical functioning, psychological wellbeing, social relationships, and reintegration alongside appropriate clinical treatment. Isolation, unnecessary inactivity, and unverified herbal treatment do not correct the fistula or address the woman's rehabilitation needs.

questions.question_text: A newborn who experienced severe birth asphyxia is later diagnosed with cerebral palsy. Which intervention is most appropriate for supporting the child's development?

choices.text: Delaying intervention until the child reaches school age
Restricting movement to prevent further neurological damage
Initiating early multidisciplinary assessment and developmentally appropriate rehabilitation
Advising the family that rehabilitation cannot improve functional ability

questions.rationale: Early intervention can support motor development, communication, feeding, positioning, and functional independence in children with cerebral palsy. Delaying assessment, restricting movement without clinical indication, and denying rehabilitation opportunities can worsen functional limitations.

questions.question_text: A mother whose infant has a congenital limb difference feels distressed and believes she caused the condition. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Tell her that she should accept the condition without discussing it
Reassure her that she is not automatically responsible and assess her emotional needs
Discourage her from holding the infant
Refer the infant for rehabilitation without involving the mother

questions.rationale: The midwife should first address maternal distress, correct misconceptions without assigning blame, and assess the mother's psychosocial needs. Excluding the mother, discouraging bonding, or dismissing her concerns undermines family-centred care.

questions.question_text: A woman recovering from an obstetric complication has completed hospital treatment but is reluctant to return to her community because of stigma. Which action best promotes successful reintegration?

choices.text: Encouraging permanent residence in the hospital
Arranging community support with her consent and addressing discriminatory attitudes
Informing community members about her diagnosis without permission
Advising her to avoid all community activities

questions.rationale: Community reintegration requires the woman's participation, respect for confidentiality, and coordinated support to reduce discrimination and promote inclusion. Permanent institutionalisation, involuntary disclosure, and social withdrawal undermine rehabilitation.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman develops lower-limb weakness following a neurological injury and requires support when walking. What should guide the selection of an assistive device?

choices.text: The cheapest device available, regardless of its suitability
The preference of the device supplier alone
A functional assessment by an appropriate rehabilitation professional
The assumption that every woman with weakness requires a wheelchair

questions.rationale: Assistive-device selection should follow an assessment of mobility, balance, strength, safety, environment, and individual needs. Cost alone, supplier preference, and assumptions about disability do not establish whether a device is clinically appropriate.

questions.question_text: A woman reports persistent urinary leakage and difficulty controlling her pelvic floor muscles after a complicated vaginal birth. Which rehabilitation service is most appropriate after clinical assessment?

choices.text: Pelvic floor rehabilitation supervised by a trained professional
Routine restriction of all fluid intake
Permanent avoidance of walking and exercise
Use of antibiotics without evidence of infection

questions.rationale: Pelvic floor rehabilitation can improve muscle function and support recovery from pelvic floor dysfunction when appropriately assessed and supervised. Fluid restriction, unnecessary inactivity, and antibiotics without evidence of infection do not treat the underlying muscular problem.

questions.question_text: A mother with a physical disability is admitted for postnatal care. Which approach best reflects family-centred rehabilitation?

choices.text: Making all care decisions without consulting her
Focusing exclusively on the infant's needs
Involving the mother in care planning and identifying support needed for infant care
Assuming that she cannot breastfeed or care for her infant

questions.rationale: Family-centred rehabilitation recognises the mother as an active decision-maker and considers her abilities, preferences, infant-care needs, and family support. Excluding her from decisions or assuming incapacity because of disability violates individualised care.

questions.question_text: During a community health session, a midwife notices that women with disabilities are rarely invited to maternal health activities. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Organising accessible sessions and involving women with disabilities in planning
Creating separate activities without consulting the women concerned
Limiting participation to women without mobility difficulties
Assuming that women with disabilities do not require maternal health education

questions.rationale: Inclusive community health programmes should remove physical, communication, and attitudinal barriers while involving affected women in decisions. Exclusion and decisions made without consultation reinforce discrimination and restrict access to care.

questions.question_text: A woman with an obstetric fistula has completed treatment and is preparing to return home. Which community-level intervention is most likely to sustain her recovery?

choices.text: A coordinated follow-up plan involving the health facility and community support services
Ending all contact with the health facility after discharge
Keeping her diagnosis secret from every healthcare professional involved in follow-up
Discouraging her from attending future reproductive health services

questions.rationale: Continuity of care links facility-based treatment with follow-up, psychosocial support, and community rehabilitation. Ending follow-up or discouraging reproductive healthcare increases the risk of unmet physical and social needs.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman with a spinal cord injury is unable to transfer independently from her bed to a chair and develops redness over her sacral area. What should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Encouraging her to remain in the same position to avoid discomfort
Assessing the skin, relieving pressure, and arranging appropriate rehabilitation support
Applying vigorous massage over the reddened area
Withholding food until she becomes independently mobile

questions.rationale: Persistent redness may indicate early pressure injury, requiring prompt skin assessment, pressure relief, repositioning, and an appropriate care plan. Prolonged pressure and vigorous massage over vulnerable skin can worsen tissue damage, while food restriction is inappropriate.

questions.question_text: A mother attending a child welfare clinic reports that her infant is not responding to sounds and is not developing age-appropriate communication skills. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Reassure her that hearing difficulties always resolve without intervention
Advise her to wait until the child starts school
Arrange prompt hearing assessment and referral for early intervention
Recommend stopping all immunisations until hearing improves

questions.rationale: Suspected hearing impairment requires prompt assessment because early identification and intervention support language and communication development. Delayed referral and discontinuation of immunisation do not address the suspected impairment.

questions.question_text: A mother with visual impairment is preparing to breastfeed her newborn. Which nursing intervention best promotes safe and independent breastfeeding?

choices.text: Assisting with positioning when needed and providing verbal guidance based on her preferences
Prohibiting breastfeeding because she cannot see the infant
Requiring a relative to perform every feeding
Separating the infant from the mother during all feeding sessions

questions.rationale: Individualised positioning support and clear verbal guidance can help a mother with visual impairment breastfeed safely and independently. Disability alone is not a reason to prohibit breastfeeding or unnecessarily separate the mother and infant.

questions.question_text: A community midwife discovers that a woman with a disability has missed antenatal appointments because the clinic entrance has stairs and no accessible alternative. Which action should take priority?

choices.text: Classifying the woman as non-compliant and closing her antenatal record
Arranging accessible care and escalating the environmental barrier to facility management
Advising her to attend only when a relative can carry her
Removing her from the maternal health programme

questions.rationale: The missed appointments are associated with an environmental access barrier, so the midwife should facilitate accessible care and advocate for corrective action. Labelling the woman non-compliant or excluding her transfers responsibility for the system's failure to the client.

questions.question_text: A woman develops severe postpartum weakness on one side of her body, facial asymmetry, and difficulty speaking. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Refer her for routine physiotherapy at her next postnatal appointment
Administer oral fluids and observe her for several hours
Activate emergency assessment and arrange urgent transfer for suspected stroke
Begin home-based exercises before obtaining medical assessment

questions.rationale: Sudden unilateral weakness, facial asymmetry, and speech difficulty suggest an acute stroke requiring emergency assessment and time-sensitive treatment. Routine rehabilitation, oral fluids, and unsupervised exercises would dangerously delay emergency care.

questions.question_text: A mother with limited mobility is discharged with a wheelchair, but her home has a narrow doorway and an uneven entrance. What should the community rehabilitation team prioritise?

choices.text: Advising her to abandon wheelchair use
Assessing the home environment and planning appropriate accessibility modifications
Recommending that she remain indoors permanently
Replacing the wheelchair without assessing the home

questions.rationale: The effectiveness of an assistive device depends partly on whether the environment permits its safe use. Assessing access barriers and planning suitable modifications addresses the actual problem, whereas abandoning mobility support or restricting participation reduces independence.

questions.question_text: A mother of a child with developmental delay reports that relatives have advised her to conceal the child's condition because of community stigma. Which response should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Supporting the family with accurate information, confidential counselling, and referral for developmental assessment
Agreeing that the child should not attend community activities
Publicly announcing the child's diagnosis to correct community attitudes
Advising the mother to discontinue developmental follow-up

questions.rationale: The midwife should support the family, protect confidentiality, encourage early assessment, and promote the child's inclusion. Social exclusion, public disclosure without consent, and discontinuing follow-up can harm the child's development and dignity.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the role of the family in community-based rehabilitation of a mother recovering from an obstetric complication?

choices.text: The family should replace all professional rehabilitation services
The family should participate in agreed care activities while respecting the woman's autonomy
Only the husband should make rehabilitation decisions
Family involvement should be avoided in every rehabilitation programme

questions.rationale: Family members can support daily activities, emotional recovery, and continuity of rehabilitation while the woman remains central to decisions. Replacing professional care, limiting decision-making to one relative, or excluding supportive family involvement undermines effective rehabilitation.

questions.question_text: A woman recovering from a severe obstetric injury wishes to return to her income-generating activities but experiences fatigue and reduced mobility. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Recommending immediate return to her previous workload without assessment
Supporting a gradual return based on functional assessment and her rehabilitation goals
Advising her to abandon employment permanently
Withholding rehabilitation until she resumes work

questions.rationale: A graded return to work should reflect the woman's functional capacity, safety, and personal goals. Immediate unrestricted work may worsen symptoms, while permanent exclusion from employment is unnecessary and delays rehabilitation.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman with a disability develops breathlessness, chest pain, and sudden swelling of one leg during a community follow-up visit. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Arrange routine rehabilitation review within one month
Massage the swollen leg to improve circulation
Arrange emergency medical assessment for suspected venous thromboembolism
Advise prolonged bed rest at home without assessment

questions.rationale: Sudden breathlessness and chest pain with unilateral leg swelling may indicate venous thromboembolism with pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening. Massage and delayed routine follow-up are unsafe, and emergency assessment is required.

topics: Herbal Medicine in Pregnancy and Lactation

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine in Pregnancy and Lactation
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman attending an antenatal clinic reports taking an herbal preparation supplied by a traditional healer to prevent miscarriage. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Immediately dismiss her beliefs and terminate the consultation
Ask about the preparation, its ingredients, dosage, and frequency of use, then assess potential risks
Advise her to double the dose if she experiences abdominal discomfort
Assure her that all natural preparations are safe during pregnancy

questions.rationale: A detailed, non-judgemental medication history helps identify possible toxicity, interactions, and pregnancy-related risks before counselling and appropriate clinical assessment. Natural products are not automatically safe, and increasing an unknown preparation's dose may expose the mother and fetus to harm.

questions.question_text: A traditional birth attendant assisting a woman in labour notices that the umbilical cord is visible at the vaginal opening. What should be the immediate priority?

choices.text: Encouraging the woman to push forcefully
Attempting to push the cord back into the uterus
Activating emergency referral for suspected cord prolapse while relieving cord compression using appropriate measures
Waiting until the next contraction before contacting a health facility

questions.rationale: Visible cord during labour suggests cord prolapse, which can rapidly compromise fetal oxygenation and requires emergency obstetric management. Pushing, manipulating the cord into the uterus, or delaying referral can worsen compression and endanger the fetus.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman tells the midwife that her family intends to apply a hot herbal mixture directly to her perineal wound. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Explain the risk of burns, contamination, and delayed healing, and discuss safer perineal care
Encourage the practice because heat always prevents infection
Advise her to stop washing the perineum completely
Recommend applying the mixture more frequently to accelerate healing

questions.rationale: An unsterile hot mixture may cause burns, introduce infection, and interfere with wound healing, so the midwife should explain the risks and provide safe care guidance. Heat does not guarantee infection prevention, and avoiding perineal hygiene or increasing exposure is unsafe.

questions.question_text: A woman receiving prescribed medication for hypertension during pregnancy reports taking an herbal product at the same time. Why is this information clinically important?

choices.text: Herbal products can interact with prescribed medicines and alter their effects or toxicity
Herbal products always strengthen antihypertensive medicines safely
Herbal products cannot contain pharmacologically active substances
Interactions occur only when medicines are given intravenously

questions.rationale: Herbal preparations may contain active substances that alter drug absorption, metabolism, blood pressure effects, or toxicity. They cannot be assumed to strengthen treatment safely, and interactions are not limited to intravenous medicines.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman declines a recommended maternity intervention because her cultural beliefs differ from the proposed treatment. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Threaten to withdraw all maternity services
Respectfully explore her concerns, explain the benefits and risks, and support informed decision-making
Proceed with the intervention without consent
Tell her that cultural beliefs have no place in maternity care

questions.rationale: Culturally safe care requires respectful communication, accurate information, and informed consent while protecting maternal and fetal wellbeing. Coercion, treatment without consent, and dismissive communication undermine autonomy and trust.

questions.question_text: A traditional birth attendant in a rural Ghanaian community wants to contribute to safer maternity care. Which role is most appropriate within a collaborative referral system?

choices.text: Managing all complicated deliveries independently
Encouraging early antenatal attendance, recognising danger signs, and facilitating timely referral
Replacing skilled birth attendants in emergency obstetric care
Administering prescription medicines without clinical authorisation

questions.rationale: Traditional birth attendants can support health education, early recognition of danger signs, and timely referral when integrated appropriately with the health system. They should not independently manage complications or undertake interventions beyond their training and authority.

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine in Pregnancy and Lactation
questions.question_text: A breastfeeding mother asks whether she can take an unidentified herbal mixture to increase breast milk production. What should the midwife advise?

choices.text: Use twice the recommended amount because lactation requires extra fluid
Avoid assessment because herbal products do not enter breast milk
Do not use the unidentified product until its safety has been assessed, and assess breastfeeding technique and milk transfer
Stop breastfeeding immediately and substitute water for breast milk

questions.rationale: The safety of an unidentified herbal product during lactation cannot be established, and active substances may pass into breast milk or affect maternal health. Assessing attachment, positioning, feeding frequency, and milk transfer addresses common breastfeeding difficulties without unnecessary exposure.

questions.question_text: A woman on the second day after delivery has heavy vaginal bleeding and dizziness. Her relatives want to give her a traditional drink before seeking medical attention. What should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Allowing the family to administer the drink before reassessment
Arranging immediate emergency assessment and management for suspected postpartum haemorrhage
Advising the woman to sleep and reassess the bleeding the next morning
Recommending abdominal massage by an untrained relative

questions.rationale: Heavy postpartum bleeding with dizziness may indicate postpartum haemorrhage and circulatory compromise, requiring immediate emergency management. Traditional drinks, delayed reassessment, and untrained abdominal manipulation must not postpone life-saving care.

questions.question_text: A traditional healer offers a pregnant woman a treatment but cannot identify its ingredients. Which concern should guide the midwife's counselling?

choices.text: The preparation may have unknown pharmacological effects, contamination, or toxicity
Unknown ingredients guarantee that the product is ineffective
The preparation is safe because it has been used for generations
The preparation cannot affect pregnancy unless it is injected

questions.rationale: Unidentified preparations create uncertainty about dose, active ingredients, contamination, and potential maternal or fetal toxicity. Traditional use does not establish safety, and substances taken orally can still have clinically significant effects.

questions.question_text: A woman receiving oxytocin for active management of the third stage of labour asks whether she should also take an herbal preparation intended to increase uterine contractions. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Approve the combination because two uterotonic substances are always more effective
Advise her to take the herbal preparation after every contraction
Avoid the unverified preparation and explain that its effects and interaction with prescribed uterotonics are unknown
Stop oxytocin and replace it with the herbal preparation

questions.rationale: An unverified uterotonic preparation may have unpredictable effects and could increase the risk of excessive uterine activity or other adverse reactions. Prescribed oxytocin should not be replaced or combined with an unknown product without appropriate clinical evidence and authorisation.

questions.question_text: A woman requests the presence of a female family elder during labour because this is important to her cultural beliefs. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Refuse the request without discussion
Accommodate the request where feasible, while maintaining privacy, safety, and the woman's consent
Allow the elder to make all clinical decisions
Permit the elder to perform clinical procedures without assessment of competence

questions.rationale: Respectful maternity care accommodates cultural preferences when they are compatible with safety, privacy, and the woman's wishes. A support person does not replace the woman's decision-making authority or the professional responsibilities of the midwife.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman receiving care from a traditional birth attendant develops severe headache, blurred vision, and epigastric pain. What should happen first?

choices.text: She should receive an herbal drink and remain at home
She should be referred urgently to a health facility for assessment of possible severe preeclampsia
She should wait until labour begins before seeking care
The attendant should encourage vigorous walking to reduce blood pressure

questions.rationale: Severe headache, visual disturbance, and epigastric pain are danger signs that may indicate severe preeclampsia and require urgent facility assessment. Home remedies, waiting for labour, and physical exertion do not treat the underlying hypertensive emergency.

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine in Pregnancy and Lactation
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman reports taking an herbal preparation and subsequently develops abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is the midwife's priority?

choices.text: Reassure her that bleeding is an expected effect of herbal treatment
Arrange urgent obstetric assessment, establish the history of the preparation, and assess maternal stability
Recommend another herbal preparation to stop the bleeding
Advise her to wait at home until the bleeding becomes heavier

questions.rationale: Abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding in pregnancy require urgent assessment for potentially serious obstetric complications, while the herbal exposure should be documented and evaluated. Reassurance, additional unverified remedies, and waiting for deterioration may delay necessary treatment.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman is being denied food and water by relatives because they believe fasting will cleanse her body after delivery. She is weak and breastfeeding. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Assess her hydration and nutritional status, then counsel the family on safe postpartum nutrition
Support continued fasting until breastfeeding is established
Advise her to stop breastfeeding to reduce nutritional requirements
Ignore the practice because family traditions cannot affect recovery

questions.rationale: The midwife should assess the woman's immediate condition and explain the importance of adequate fluids and nutrition for postpartum recovery and lactation. Prolonged food and fluid restriction may worsen dehydration, weakness, and nutritional deficiency.

questions.question_text: A midwife learns that a pregnant client has been given an herbal preparation by a relative without her knowledge. Which ethical principle is most directly involved?

choices.text: Autonomy and informed consent
Distributive justice alone
Professional delegation
Resource allocation

questions.rationale: Autonomy requires respect for the woman's right to make informed decisions about substances and interventions used in her care. Administering an unidentified preparation without her knowledge bypasses consent and may expose her to preventable harm.

questions.question_text: A woman with postpartum hypertension is taking prescribed antihypertensive medication but also uses an herbal product. Her blood pressure becomes markedly elevated. What is the best clinical response?

choices.text: Assume the herbal product is harmless and continue the same care
Stop all prescribed medication without medical review
Assess her urgently, document all products used, and arrange clinical review of treatment and possible interactions
Advise her to take additional doses of the herbal product

questions.rationale: Markedly elevated postpartum blood pressure requires prompt assessment because of the risk of serious complications, including stroke and eclampsia. Medication and herbal-product histories should be reviewed by the treating team rather than stopping prescribed treatment or increasing an unverified product independently.

questions.question_text: A traditional birth attendant has supported a woman through an uncomplicated pregnancy but the woman plans to deliver at home without a skilled birth attendant. Which message should the midwife emphasise?

choices.text: Antenatal attendance alone eliminates the need for skilled care during birth
Skilled birth attendance supports early recognition and management of maternal and newborn complications
A traditional birth attendant can provide emergency surgery if required
Emergency referral is necessary only when the mother loses consciousness

questions.rationale: Skilled birth attendance supports safe intrapartum monitoring and timely intervention when complications arise, even in pregnancies previously considered low risk. Antenatal attendance does not eliminate intrapartum risks, and referral should occur before a woman becomes critically ill.

questions.question_text: A midwife working in a rural community disagrees with a harmless cultural practice preferred by a pregnant woman. Which approach best demonstrates cultural competence?

choices.text: Prohibiting the practice because it differs from the midwife's personal beliefs
Assessing whether the practice creates clinical risk and respecting the woman's preference when it is safe
Reporting the woman for refusing modern healthcare
Ignoring the woman's explanation and continuing the consultation

questions.rationale: Cultural competence involves understanding the woman's beliefs and distinguishing harmless practices from practices that create clinical risk. Personal disagreement alone is not a reason to prohibit a safe practice or undermine respectful communication.

questions.question_text: A newborn is delivered at a health facility, is apnoeic, and has a heart rate of 80 beats per minute after initial steps of newborn resuscitation. What should the midwife do next?

choices.text: Begin effective positive-pressure ventilation
Start chest compressions immediately without ventilation
Observe for five minutes before intervening
Administer oral glucose

questions.rationale: Apnoea with a heart rate below 100 beats per minute after initial steps indicates the need for effective positive-pressure ventilation. Chest compressions are considered only when the heart rate remains below 60 beats per minute after at least 30 seconds of effective ventilation.

questions.question_text: A newborn develops visible jaundice eight hours after birth. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Reassure the mother that all newborn jaundice is physiological
Arrange urgent clinical assessment and bilirubin measurement
Recommend exposing the newborn to direct sunlight as the only treatment
Stop breastfeeding immediately without assessment

questions.rationale: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours is potentially pathological and requires urgent evaluation to identify the cause and assess bilirubin levels. Routine reassurance, sunlight as a substitute for treatment, and unnecessary interruption of breastfeeding can delay appropriate management.

questions.question_text: A clinically stable preterm infant is admitted to the neonatal unit and weighs 1.7 kg. Which intervention is particularly beneficial for maintaining warmth and supporting breastfeeding?

choices.text: Routine separation from the mother
Kangaroo mother care with appropriate monitoring
Bathing the infant immediately after admission
Giving water between breastfeeds

questions.rationale: Kangaroo mother care provides sustained skin-to-skin contact, supports thermal regulation, and promotes breastfeeding in eligible low-birth-weight infants. Unnecessary separation, early bathing, and water supplementation increase risks without providing the benefits of kangaroo mother care.

questions.question_text: A three-day-old newborn develops poor feeding, lethargy, temperature instability, and respiratory distress. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Arrange urgent neonatal assessment and initiate the facility's sepsis management pathway
Advise the mother to increase feeding and return after two days
Administer an unprescribed herbal preparation
Discharge the newborn because temperature instability is normal

questions.rationale: Poor feeding, lethargy, temperature instability, and respiratory distress are danger signs of possible neonatal sepsis requiring urgent assessment and treatment. Delayed review, unprescribed remedies, and discharge can lead to rapid deterioration.

questions.question_text: A newborn of a mother with diabetes becomes jittery and feeds poorly two hours after birth. Which condition should the midwife suspect first?

choices.text: Neonatal hypoglycaemia
Physiological weight loss only
Normal neonatal sleep behaviour
Uncomplicated neonatal jaundice

questions.rationale: Infants of mothers with diabetes are at increased risk of neonatal hypoglycaemia, which may present with jitteriness and poor feeding. These findings require prompt blood glucose assessment and appropriate management rather than reassurance or attribution to unrelated conditions.

questions.question_text: A mother brings her six-week-old infant to a child welfare clinic in Ghana. Which activity is an important part of the visit?

choices.text: Assessing growth and development, reviewing immunisation status, and providing caregiver education
Giving antibiotics routinely to prevent childhood infections
Withholding all vaccines until the child starts school
Assessing weight only and omitting feeding history

questions.rationale: Well-baby care includes growth monitoring, developmental surveillance, immunisation according to the national schedule, and caregiver education. Routine antibiotics, unnecessary vaccine delays, and assessment limited to weight do not provide comprehensive preventive care.

questions.question_text: A mother reports that her nine-month-old infant cannot sit without support and has poor head control. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Dismiss the concern because all children develop at the same rate
Arrange developmental assessment and appropriate referral
Advise the mother to stop interacting with the infant
Wait until the child is three years old before assessing development

questions.rationale: Poor head control and inability to sit independently at this age warrant developmental assessment to identify possible neurological or developmental problems. Dismissing the concern or delaying assessment can prevent timely intervention.

questions.question_text: During newborn resuscitation, the heart rate remains at 50 beats per minute after 30 seconds of effective positive-pressure ventilation that visibly moves the chest. What should the resuscitation team do next?

choices.text: Stop ventilation and observe for spontaneous recovery
Initiate chest compressions coordinated with ventilation
Give oral feeds immediately
Discontinue resuscitation because the newborn has a heartbeat

questions.rationale: A heart rate below 60 beats per minute despite at least 30 seconds of effective ventilation indicates the need for chest compressions coordinated with ventilation under the neonatal resuscitation algorithm. Stopping ventilation or giving oral feeds would interrupt life-saving resuscitation.

questions.question_text: A preterm infant is placed in an open cot after delivery and begins to develop cold extremities and a low body temperature. Which action should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Remove the infant's clothing to improve ventilation
Provide appropriate thermal support and monitor the infant's temperature
Delay intervention until the next feeding
Bathe the infant to stimulate circulation

questions.rationale: Preterm infants have limited thermal regulation and are at high risk of hypothermia, so immediate warming and temperature monitoring are essential. Removing clothing, delaying care, or bathing the infant increases heat loss.

questions.question_text: A newborn receiving phototherapy for significant hyperbilirubinaemia is being monitored. Which nursing action is essential?

choices.text: Ensure appropriate eye protection and monitor temperature, hydration, and bilirubin response
Cover the entire body with thick clothing during treatment
Stop all feeding throughout phototherapy
Apply herbal oil to the skin before each treatment session

questions.rationale: Phototherapy requires appropriate eye protection according to equipment guidance, adequate skin exposure, temperature and hydration monitoring, and assessment of bilirubin response. Thick clothing reduces treatment exposure, while stopping feeds and applying unverified products can compromise care.

questions.question_text: A newborn develops grunting, chest indrawing, and central cyanosis in the postnatal ward. What should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Immediate assessment and emergency support for respiratory compromise
Routine weighing before clinical assessment
Oral feeding to improve energy levels
Waiting for the paediatric ward round

questions.rationale: Grunting, chest indrawing, and central cyanosis indicate severe respiratory compromise requiring immediate assessment and emergency intervention. Feeding, routine weighing, and waiting for a later review delay treatment of a potentially life-threatening condition.

questions.question_text: A newborn at risk of hypoglycaemia is being assessed after delivery. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Initiate early feeding when clinically appropriate and monitor blood glucose according to protocol
Give plain water before the first breastfeed
Delay feeding until the infant cries persistently
Avoid glucose monitoring in infants who appear well

questions.rationale: Early feeding and protocol-based glucose monitoring help prevent and detect hypoglycaemia in at-risk newborns. Water and delayed feeding provide no appropriate preventive benefit, and an apparently well infant may still have low blood glucose.

questions.question_text: A mother presents her infant for immunisation and reports that the child developed a mild fever after the previous vaccine dose. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Assess the child's current condition and explain expected minor reactions and danger signs
Declare that all future vaccines are permanently contraindicated
Recommend antibiotics before every vaccine dose
Advise the mother to conceal future reactions

questions.rationale: Mild fever can occur after immunisation and should be assessed alongside the child's current condition and any history suggesting a serious adverse event. A mild reaction alone does not establish a permanent contraindication or justify routine antibiotic use.

questions.question_text: A vigorous term newborn is delivered with a strong cry and good muscle tone. Which immediate approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Routine separation for suctioning of the airway
Provide routine care, maintain warmth, and support early skin-to-skin contact
Begin positive-pressure ventilation
Perform routine deep suctioning before assessing breathing

questions.rationale: A vigorous newborn who is breathing or crying and has good tone generally requires routine care, thermal protection, and early skin-to-skin contact. Routine ventilation or suctioning is unnecessary and may interfere with normal transition and bonding.

questions.question_text: A newborn has jaundice, poor feeding, and increasing lethargy. The mother asks to take the infant home because the yellow colour is becoming less noticeable. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Discharge the infant because skin colour appears improved
Arrange urgent assessment of bilirubin and the infant's clinical condition
Recommend direct sunlight and review after one week
Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding permanently

questions.rationale: Poor feeding and lethargy in a jaundiced newborn may indicate significant hyperbilirubinaemia or another serious illness and require urgent assessment. Apparent improvement in skin colour does not reliably establish safety, and delayed review or unnecessary breastfeeding cessation is inappropriate.

questions.question_text: A preterm newborn is breathing spontaneously but has poor feeding and recurrent episodes of apnoea. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Transfer the infant to a routine postnatal cot without monitoring
Arrange urgent neonatal review and appropriate respiratory and feeding support
Give large volumes of oral milk to prevent apnoea
Discontinue temperature monitoring

questions.rationale: Recurrent apnoea and poor feeding in a preterm infant may indicate significant respiratory or systemic illness requiring urgent neonatal assessment and monitoring. Unmonitored routine care and large oral feeds may increase risk, particularly if coordination of sucking and swallowing is impaired.

questions.question_text: A mother attending a child welfare clinic reports that her 18-month-old child has lost previously acquired words and no longer responds consistently to her name. What is the best response?

choices.text: Explain that loss of acquired skills is a reason for prompt developmental assessment and referral
Reassure her that regression is always a normal stage of development
Advise her to stop speaking to the child
Wait until the child reaches primary school before seeking assessment

questions.rationale: Loss of previously acquired developmental skills is a significant concern requiring prompt assessment and referral. Dismissing regression or delaying evaluation can postpone identification of neurological, developmental, or hearing-related conditions.

topics: Safe Motherhood and Skilled Birth Attendance

questions.question_text: During an antenatal education session at a CHPS compound, a pregnant woman asks why she should attend antenatal care when she feels healthy. Which explanation is most appropriate?

choices.text: Antenatal care identifies potential complications, supports preventive interventions, and promotes maternal and fetal wellbeing
Antenatal care is required only when labour begins
Antenatal care guarantees that complications cannot occur
Antenatal care replaces the need for skilled birth attendance

questions.rationale: Antenatal care provides screening, preventive interventions, health education, and opportunities for early identification of maternal and fetal risks. It does not guarantee a complication-free pregnancy or replace skilled care during childbirth.

questions.topic: Safe Motherhood and Skilled Birth Attendance
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman with a history of severe preeclampsia in a previous pregnancy is planning to deliver at home. What should the community midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Encouraging home delivery because the previous pregnancy has ended
Developing an individualised birth and referral plan that includes skilled facility-based care
Advising her to avoid antenatal care until labour starts
Recommending traditional treatment as a substitute for emergency obstetric care

questions.rationale: A history of severe preeclampsia identifies a woman who requires appropriate risk assessment, monitoring, and a clear plan for skilled childbirth and emergency referral. Home delivery without appropriate skilled support may delay recognition and treatment of recurrent complications.

questions.question_text: A community midwife conducts a postnatal home visit and finds that a mother has fever, lower abdominal pain, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Advise the mother to take herbal preparations and rest
Arrange urgent clinical assessment for possible puerperal infection
Reassure her that fever is always normal after childbirth
Delay review until the routine six-week postnatal visit

questions.rationale: Fever, lower abdominal pain, and foul-smelling lochia suggest possible postpartum infection and require prompt assessment and treatment. Herbal remedies and delayed review may allow infection to progress to severe sepsis.

questions.question_text: A woman attending her postnatal visit says she wants to delay another pregnancy for at least three years. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Provide balanced counselling on suitable postpartum contraceptive methods and support informed choice
Select a method without explaining alternatives
Tell her that contraception is unnecessary while breastfeeding
Advise her to wait until menstruation returns before discussing contraception

questions.rationale: Postpartum family planning counselling should address the woman's reproductive intentions, medical eligibility, breastfeeding status, and preferences. Breastfeeding does not automatically prevent pregnancy, and counselling should not be delayed until menstruation resumes.

questions.question_text: A CHPS nurse identifies a pregnant woman with severe headache, visual disturbance, and markedly elevated blood pressure. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Arrange urgent referral for assessment and management of possible severe preeclampsia
Schedule another blood pressure check in one month
Recommend increased physical activity
Advise the woman to reduce water intake and remain at home

questions.rationale: Severe hypertension with neurological symptoms may indicate severe preeclampsia and requires urgent facility-based assessment and management. Routine follow-up and home advice alone risk delaying treatment of a potentially life-threatening complication.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse learns that a pregnant woman has not attended antenatal care because her family cannot afford transport to the health facility. Which public health response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Label the woman as irresponsible and discontinue follow-up
Assess the access barrier and coordinate community support and referral arrangements
Wait until the woman presents in labour
Advise the family to use unverified medicines instead of antenatal care

questions.rationale: Public health nursing addresses barriers to healthcare access through community engagement, referral coordination, and appropriate support arrangements. Blaming the woman or waiting until labour does not address the transport barrier or protect maternal health.

questions.question_text: Which intervention is a central component of promoting exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months of an infant's life?

choices.text: Giving water between breastfeeds in hot weather
Providing breastfeeding support, including correct attachment and positioning
Introducing cereal at two months
Replacing night feeds with sweetened water

questions.rationale: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months means providing breast milk without other foods or drinks, except prescribed medicines, vitamins, minerals, or oral rehydration solution when indicated. Water, early cereal, and sweetened drinks undermine exclusive breastfeeding and may increase infection risk.

questions.topic: Safe Motherhood and Skilled Birth Attendance
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman in a remote community develops heavy vaginal bleeding before delivery. Which action should the community midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Arrange emergency referral while initiating appropriate stabilisation within available capacity
Wait for the bleeding to stop spontaneously
Encourage the woman to walk to the health facility
Administer an unprescribed herbal preparation

questions.rationale: Antepartum haemorrhage is an obstetric emergency requiring urgent assessment, referral, and appropriate stabilisation. Waiting, encouraging unnecessary exertion, or using unverified remedies can worsen maternal and fetal outcomes.

questions.question_text: A woman who delivered two weeks ago reports persistent sadness, loss of interest, and difficulty caring for herself and her infant. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Dismiss the symptoms as ordinary maternal tiredness
Assess her mental health and safety, including thoughts of self-harm, and arrange appropriate support
Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately
Tell her that mental health concerns should not be discussed during postnatal care

questions.rationale: Persistent depressive symptoms may indicate a postpartum mental health disorder and require assessment of severity, functioning, and immediate safety. Dismissing symptoms or avoiding mental health assessment may leave the mother and infant at risk.

questions.question_text: A community midwife receives information that a woman who delivered at home died following severe bleeding. Which public health action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore the report because the delivery did not occur in a facility
Ensure the death is reported through the appropriate channels and support the maternal death review process
Discuss the woman's identity publicly to discourage home delivery
Alter the cause of death to avoid criticism of the community

questions.rationale: Maternal deaths require appropriate notification, documentation, and review to identify preventable factors and improve the health system. Ignoring the death, breaching confidentiality, or falsifying records undermines surveillance and accountability.

questions.question_text: A pregnant adolescent at a CHPS compound reports that she has been denied antenatal care by relatives because of her age. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Provide respectful, confidential, age-appropriate care and facilitate access to antenatal services
Refuse care until her relatives approve
Refer her away without assessment because she is an adolescent
Disclose her pregnancy to community members without consent

questions.rationale: Adolescents require respectful, non-discriminatory maternity care, with confidentiality and safeguarding handled according to applicable law and professional standards. Refusal of care and unnecessary disclosure can increase barriers and expose the young woman to harm.

questions.question_text: During a group antenatal session, a woman asks which symptoms should prompt immediate assessment during pregnancy. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Severe headache, visual disturbance, vaginal bleeding, convulsions, or reduced fetal movement
Mild hunger before meals and occasional fetal hiccups
Normal breast enlargement and gradual abdominal growth
Increased appetite and mild fatigue after activity

questions.rationale: Severe headache, visual disturbance, bleeding, convulsions, and reduced fetal movement are important danger signs requiring prompt assessment. Normal physiological changes and mild symptoms without warning features do not carry the same immediate concern.

questions.topic: Safe Motherhood and Skilled Birth Attendance
questions.question_text: A woman in labour at a peripheral health facility develops signs of obstructed labour, and the facility lacks the capacity for operative delivery. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Continue augmentation without reassessing the cause of obstruction
Arrange urgent referral to a facility with comprehensive emergency obstetric care while providing appropriate stabilisation
Encourage forceful pushing regardless of cervical dilatation
Discharge the woman to deliver at home

questions.rationale: Suspected obstructed labour requires urgent assessment and referral to a facility capable of providing the necessary emergency obstetric intervention. Unsupervised augmentation, forceful pushing, and discharge may cause uterine rupture, fetal compromise, and maternal injury.

questions.question_text: A woman on the fifth postpartum day suddenly develops breathlessness, chest pain, and collapse. What should the community midwife do first?

choices.text: Arrange emergency medical response for suspected pulmonary embolism
Recommend oral fluids and routine review the following week
Encourage walking to relieve the chest pain
Assume the symptoms are caused by normal postpartum fatigue

questions.rationale: Sudden breathlessness, chest pain, and collapse in the postpartum period may indicate pulmonary embolism, a life-threatening emergency. Routine review, oral fluids alone, and encouraging exertion would dangerously delay emergency care.

questions.question_text: A district health team notices that maternal health education sessions are attended mainly by women from nearby communities, while remote communities have low participation. Which strategy is most appropriate?

choices.text: Concentrating all sessions at the district hospital
Using community outreach, local engagement, and CHPS structures to improve access
Stopping education sessions in communities with low attendance
Restricting education to women who have already delivered in a facility

questions.rationale: Outreach and CHPS-based engagement can reduce geographical and access barriers and improve participation in maternal health education. Centralising services or excluding underserved communities increases inequity rather than addressing the reasons for low attendance.

questions.question_text: A community midwife identifies several pregnant women who have missed scheduled antenatal appointments. What is the most appropriate first step in planning follow-up?

choices.text: Determine the reasons for missed visits and assess whether any woman has an urgent health concern
Remove all the women from the antenatal register
Assume that all the women have relocated
Wait until the women independently return to the clinic

questions.rationale: Follow-up should establish why appointments were missed and identify women who may require urgent assessment or assistance accessing care. Removing records or making assumptions can result in missed opportunities for early intervention.

questions.question_text: A mother attending a postnatal clinic asks when complementary foods should generally be introduced to a healthy infant who is exclusively breastfed. What should the midwife explain?

choices.text: At two months
At four months
At six months, while breastfeeding continues
At twelve months, with no other food before then

questions.rationale: Complementary feeding should generally begin at six months while breastfeeding continues, with age-appropriate, nutritionally adequate foods. Introducing foods too early may increase infection and feeding risks, while delaying beyond six months can compromise nutritional adequacy.

questions.topic: Safe Motherhood and Skilled Birth Attendance
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman with a known high-risk condition is booked at a CHPS compound but has no documented plan for emergency transport or referral. What should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Developing a birth preparedness and complication readiness plan with clear referral arrangements
Assuming that the condition will resolve during labour
Advising the woman to avoid discussing the condition with family members
Waiting until an emergency develops before identifying a referral facility

questions.rationale: Birth preparedness and complication readiness include identifying a suitable delivery facility, transport, emergency contacts, and financial arrangements where relevant. Waiting for an emergency to develop can delay access to life-saving obstetric care.

questions.question_text: A midwife who owns a private maternity clinic wants to advertise her services on social media. Which statement is most ethically appropriate?

choices.text: Our clinic guarantees normal delivery for every pregnant woman
Our maternity services include antenatal assessment, skilled birth care, and appropriate referral when complications arise
Choose our clinic because complications never occur under our care
Women who attend other clinics are more likely to experience poor outcomes

questions.rationale: Ethical marketing provides accurate information about available services without promising outcomes that cannot be guaranteed. Claims that complications never occur or that competitors cause poor outcomes are misleading and may undermine informed choice.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman tells a midwife that she is considering changing facilities because she feels her concerns are ignored. What should the midwife do first?

choices.text: Listen actively, acknowledge her concerns, and discuss how her care can be improved
Tell her that she must remain with the facility
Threaten to discontinue her antenatal services
Ignore the complaint because she has already registered

questions.rationale: Active listening and respectful communication help identify service failures and rebuild trust in the client relationship. Coercion, threats, and ignoring complaints damage trust and violate respectful maternity care principles.

questions.question_text: A midwife wants to post a photograph of a newborn and the mother's delivery experience on the clinic's social media page. What must happen before publication?

choices.text: The midwife should publish the photograph because the delivery occurred at her clinic
The mother and any other relevant rights-holder should provide valid informed consent, with privacy safeguards observed
The photograph may be posted if the mother's face is partly covered
The midwife should ask another staff member to publish it instead

questions.rationale: Identifiable patient images and personal health information require appropriate consent and confidentiality safeguards before publication. Clinic ownership of the service or partial concealment of a face does not automatically authorise disclosure.

questions.question_text: A midwife plans to establish a private antenatal clinic in a district where several facilities already operate. What should she do before investing substantial funds?

choices.text: Conduct a market assessment to identify community needs, demand, competition, and required resources
Rent the largest available building without assessing demand
Set service fees without considering operating costs
Assume that every pregnant woman in the district will attend the new clinic

questions.rationale: A market assessment helps determine whether the proposed service addresses a genuine need and can operate sustainably within the local healthcare environment. Investing without assessing demand, costs, and competition increases financial and operational risk.

questions.question_text: A private maternity clinic has low antenatal attendance among women in nearby rural communities. Which strategy is most appropriate for improving community engagement?

choices.text: Working with community leaders and CHPS personnel to identify access barriers and provide appropriate health education
Blaming rural women for failing to value maternal health
Stopping services for women who live outside the town
Using frightening messages to pressure women into registering

questions.rationale: Community engagement should identify local needs and barriers through collaboration with trusted community structures and health personnel. Blame, exclusion, and fear-based promotion undermine trust and may discourage timely maternity care.

questions.question_text: A maternity clinic receives repeated complaints about long waiting times during antenatal visits. What should the manager do first?

choices.text: Collect and analyse waiting-time information to identify causes before selecting corrective measures
Delete all complaints from the feedback register
Increase consultation fees without reviewing the service process
Blame clients for arriving at the facility

questions.rationale: Quality improvement begins with identifying and analysing the problem using reliable service information and client feedback. Deleting complaints, increasing fees without justification, or blaming clients does not address the underlying causes of delays.

questions.question_text: A private maternity clinic receives a pregnant woman who cannot immediately pay for an emergency assessment. What should the midwife prioritise?

choices.text: Refuse all assessment until payment is completed
Assess and respond to the emergency according to professional standards, while addressing payment arrangements appropriately
Send the woman home without assessing her condition
Publicly disclose her financial situation to other clients

questions.rationale: Emergency clinical needs must be assessed and managed according to professional obligations and applicable policies, without allowing payment discussions to cause dangerous delays. Refusal of assessment and public disclosure of financial information compromise safety and dignity.

questions.question_text: A clinic advertises a maternity package as including antenatal care, delivery services, and postnatal review. Which additional information best supports informed client choice?

choices.text: Clear information about included services, exclusions, fees, and referral arrangements
A statement that the clinic's services are superior to every public hospital
A promise that clients will never need referral to another facility
An instruction that clients should not ask questions about costs

questions.rationale: Transparent information about services, costs, limitations, and referral arrangements enables clients to make informed decisions. Unsupported superiority claims, guarantees against referral, and concealment of costs are misleading and unethical.

questions.question_text: A woman complains that a midwife discussed her HIV status within hearing of other clients. What should the facility manager do first?

choices.text: Dismiss the complaint because the information was shared by a healthcare worker
Address the immediate confidentiality concern, listen to the woman, and initiate the appropriate reporting and review process
Ask the woman to apologise to the midwife
Discuss the woman's complaint during a public staff meeting using her full name

questions.rationale: Disclosure of HIV status without appropriate justification may constitute a serious confidentiality breach and requires a respectful response, protection of the woman's privacy, and appropriate review. Dismissing the complaint or repeating identifiable information compounds the breach.

questions.question_text: A midwife plans to introduce an ultrasound service in her private maternity clinic. What should be considered before implementation?

choices.text: Staff competence, equipment quality, regulatory requirements, clinical governance, and referral arrangements
The ability to advertise ultrasound as a replacement for all antenatal assessments
The number of social media followers alone
Whether the service can operate without trained personnel

questions.rationale: A new diagnostic service requires appropriate competence, equipment, governance, regulatory compliance, and pathways for clinical follow-up. Marketing reach alone does not establish safety or clinical quality, and ultrasound cannot replace comprehensive antenatal assessment.

questions.question_text: A maternity clinic wants to increase attendance among pregnant adolescents who report fear of judgement by healthcare workers. Which intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Providing adolescent-responsive services with respectful communication and appropriate confidentiality
Displaying posters that shame adolescents who become pregnant
Requiring all adolescents to attend with a public community representative
Refusing antenatal registration to unmarried adolescents

questions.rationale: Adolescent-responsive maternity services reduce stigma through respectful communication, privacy, and appropriate access to care. Shaming, unnecessary disclosure, and discrimination discourage attendance and may increase maternal and newborn risks.

questions.question_text: A maternity clinic records an increase in clients returning for postnatal review after introducing appointment reminders. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

choices.text: The increase suggests the reminders may be improving follow-up, but further monitoring is needed
The increase proves that maternal mortality has been eliminated
The increase means the clinic no longer needs to assess postnatal clients
The increase proves that every client prefers digital communication

questions.rationale: Improved attendance is a useful service indicator and may suggest that reminders are supporting continuity of care. It does not prove that mortality has been eliminated or that every client has the same communication preferences.

questions.question_text: A clinic manager asks a midwife to exaggerate the risks of public hospital delivery so that more pregnant women will register at the private clinic. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Comply because increasing clinic revenue is the main business objective
Refuse misleading promotion and provide balanced, evidence-based information about available maternity services
Publish anonymous negative stories about public hospitals
Promise that private care eliminates all obstetric complications

questions.rationale: Ethical marketing requires truthful, balanced communication and respect for the public's ability to make informed healthcare choices. Exaggerating risks, spreading unverified claims, and guaranteeing outcomes are misleading and inconsistent with professional accountability.

questions.question_text: A clinic employee sends a photograph of a client's antenatal record to a personal WhatsApp group to ask for informal advice. What should the midwife in charge do first?

choices.text: Ignore the incident because the group contains healthcare workers
Address the disclosure, protect the client's information, and follow the facility's confidentiality and incident-reporting procedures
Forward the record to a larger group for additional opinions
Delete the client's entire medical record

questions.rationale: Sharing identifiable clinical records through an unauthorised personal group may breach confidentiality and requires immediate attention, appropriate reporting, and protection of the client's information. Expanding the disclosure or deleting the official record would create further ethical and documentation problems.

questions.question_text: A clinic introduces a premium maternity package with additional amenities. A staff member begins giving clients in the premium package faster emergency assessment than clients using the standard package. What should the manager do?

choices.text: Maintain the arrangement because premium clients pay higher fees
Ensure clinical urgency, not package type, determines assessment and treatment priority
Restrict emergency care to clients with private insurance
Allow staff to decide priority according to personal preference

questions.rationale: Clinical prioritisation must be based on urgency and patient safety rather than ability to pay or service package. Giving premium clients preferential emergency assessment can delay care for critically ill women and violates equitable professional practice.

questions.question_text: A midwife operating a private clinic discovers that monthly expenses consistently exceed income. Which action should she take first?

choices.text: Review financial records, service utilisation, operating costs, and pricing before making changes
Immediately stop providing essential emergency maternity care
Increase all fees without assessing affordability or demand
Destroy financial records to avoid identifying losses

questions.rationale: A financial review identifies the sources of operating losses and supports evidence-based decisions about efficiency, service mix, and pricing. Arbitrary fee increases, stopping essential care, or destroying records undermine sustainability and accountability.

questions.question_text: A woman experiences disrespectful treatment during labour at a private maternity clinic and submits a formal complaint. Which response best supports relationship management?

choices.text: Acknowledging the complaint, listening without retaliation, investigating appropriately, and communicating corrective action
Threatening the woman with legal action for damaging the clinic's reputation
Deleting the complaint and refusing further communication
Publishing the woman's name and complaint on social media

questions.rationale: Effective relationship management requires respectful complaint handling, fair investigation, accountability, and appropriate communication about improvements. Retaliation, concealment, and public disclosure of the complainant's identity undermine trust and may breach confidentiality.

questions.question_text: A private maternity clinic wants to advertise that it accepts clients registered under the NHIS and clients using the free maternal health care policy. What should the clinic do before publishing the advertisement?

choices.text: Verify the applicable provider arrangements, covered services, eligibility conditions, and any legitimate charges
Advertise that every service is free regardless of eligibility or coverage
Promise reimbursement for every expense without checking policy requirements
Avoid explaining payment arrangements to clients

questions.rationale: Accurate advertising requires the clinic to verify its participation arrangements and explain applicable coverage, eligibility, and charges transparently. Claiming that every service is free or guaranteeing reimbursement without verification may mislead clients and create financial disputes.
